--- status: Draft owner: planning-agent updated: 2026-10-13 tags: feed, watcher --- # Live changes feed The feed answers one question: *what changed while I was looking elsewhere?* It lists every file the watcher reports, keyed by path, so a file saved twelve times stays one entry that moves back to the top. > [!NOTE] > Temporary files (`*.tmp`, `~$*`, swap files) and build folders never reach the feed. The filter runs in the core, before events are batched. ## Event model Events come from two sources. The [file watcher](watcher.md) reports single saves; the git-dir watcher reports operations such as checkout or rebase, which arrive as one bulk batch.[^1] | Event | Source | Feed | Toast | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | created | watcher | new entry | yes | | modified | watcher | updated in place | yes | | removed | watcher | kept, struck through | yes | | checkout | git operation | one collapsed entry | no | ### Sources The file watcher and the git-dir watcher are the only two sources; nothing polls. ### Batches A batch closes after 150 ms of quiet, or after one second at the most. ```ts // One batch per quiet period (150 ms), or at most every second. type FsBatch = { changes: FsChange[]; bulk: null | { count: number; reason: "gitOperation" | "large" | "overflow" }; rescan: boolean; }; ``` ## Grouping Bursts of saves collapse into one entry and **never produce more than one toast**: while a burst lasts, the toast updates its counter in place instead of stacking. Each save shows its own toast, so nothing is missed. Follow mode (Ctrl+Shift+L) opens the latest changed doc at most once every three seconds, and never for a bulk batch. > The feed is only useful if it is quiet. If people stop looking at it, it has failed. > > *Design review, 2026-10-12* ## Pipeline ```mermaid graph LR Watcher[Watcher] --> Aggregator[Aggregator] Aggregator --> Reconcile[Reconcile with disk] Reconcile --> Feed[Feed and toast] ``` ## Rollout - [x] Aggregate events (150 ms quiet, 1 s max) - [x] Reconcile with disk and drop duplicates - [x] Bulk detection for git operations - [ ] Follow dwell: at most one jump every 3 s - [ ] Worktree labels in the feed See [the old spec](../old/spec.md) for the first draft, the [lore notes](../world/lore.md#characters) for naming, or the [cost model](#cost-model) below. ## Cost model Reconciling a batch of $n$ files costs $O(n \log n)$ with the sorted merge. $$\int_0^1 x^2\,dx = \frac{1}{3}$$ A broken formula keeps its source: $\frac{1}{$. ## Notes
Bulk
A batch of more than 200 events, or any git operation.
Burst
Normal saves that arrive within ten seconds of each other.
Why not poll?

Polling wastes battery and misses short-lived files. The native watcher is cheaper and exact.

> [!TIP] > Use F7 to jump between the blocks that just changed. > [!WARNING] > Large checkouts can touch thousands of files; they are grouped on purpose. > [!CAUTION] > Do not edit `.trailmark/cache` by hand. > [!IMPORTANT] > The feed is keyed by path: renames move the entry, they do not duplicate it. The pipeline in one picture: ![Pipeline diagram](../images/pipeline.svg) H2O and E = mc2, plus ~~strikethrough~~ and an autolink: [https://example.com/feed](https://example.com/feed). [^1]: Git operations are detected from the git directory, not from the file events.

# Watcher

The watcher turns raw file events into batches for the [feed](live-feed.md#event-model). See also the [research notes](../research/watchers.md).

## Debounce

Events are held for 150 ms of quiet, with a hard limit of one second, then reconciled with the disk.

```rust
fn flush(&mut self) -> Vec<FsChange> {
    // reconcile with disk: stat + hash, drop duplicates
    self.pending.drain().filter(|c| c.changed()).collect()
}
```

## Limits

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| quiet period | 150 ms |
| max wait | 1 s |
| bulk threshold | 200 events |

# Lore

Notes on the people and places of the series. Keep this file the single source of truth.

## Characters

Character notes: tall, quiet, a cartographer who trusts maps more than people. Her descriptions change per book as she ages.

### Aria

Aria carries a brass compass. Physical **descriptions** must stay consistent with book one: grey eyes, a scar over the left brow.

### Bram

The character sheet lists his scars in order. Keep descriptions short; the narrator never describes him twice in one chapter.

## World

The coast is mapped in three layers: the harbor charts, the inland roads and the old tunnels. Each layer has its own style guide.

## Magic

Magic costs memory. Every spell removes one concrete detail from the caster's past, which is why descriptions of old places grow vague.

```yaml
cost:
  memory: 1
  recoverable: false
```

# Reading width

Text reads best in a column of about seventy characters, so paragraphs, lists, headings and quotes stay at the measure. Tables, code, diagrams, formulas and pictures often need more room than that, and they are allowed to take it.

## A table that needs room

| Event | Source | Debounce | Grouping | Feed row | Toast | Follow | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| created | file watcher | 150 ms | by path | new entry | yes | yes | A new file is a changed file. |
| modified | file watcher | 150 ms | by path | updated in place | yes | yes | Twelve saves stay one row. |
| removed | file watcher | 150 ms | by path | kept, struck through | yes | no | The row stays until the next scan. |
| checkout | git operation | none | one bulk batch | one collapsed row | no | no | Never produces a toast or a jump. |

A narrow table stays at the measure, because its content does not need more.

| Mode | Width |
| --- | --- |
| Comfortable | 760 px |
| Wide | 1100 px |
| Full | the pane |

## A long line of code

```ts
const summary = events.filter((event) => event.kind !== 'removed').map((event) => ({ path: event.path, at: event.atMs, group: groupOf(event), hidden: isHiddenByFilter(event.path) })).sort((a, b) => b.at - a.at);
```

Short code stays at the measure too.

```ts
const answer = 42;
```

## A diagram

```mermaid
graph LR
  Watcher[File watcher] --> Debounce[Debounce 150 ms] --> Group[Group by path] --> Reconcile[Reconcile with disk] --> Feed[Feed row] --> Toast[Toast] --> Follow[Follow jump] --> Outline[Outline update]
```

## A formula

$$S_n = \sum_{k=1}^{n} \frac{(-1)^{k+1}}{k} \cdot \left(\frac{a_k + b_k + c_k + d_k + e_k + f_k + g_k + h_k + i_k + j_k + l_k + m_k}{\sqrt{1 + x_k^2 + y_k^2 + z_k^2}}\right) + \int_0^\infty \frac{e^{-t}}{1 + t^2}\,dt$$

## A wide picture

![An image 1000 px wide](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D%22http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg%22%20width%3D%221000%22%20height%3D%22160%22%20viewBox%3D%220%200%201000%20160%22%3E%3Crect%20width%3D%221000%22%20height%3D%22160%22%20rx%3D%2212%22%20fill%3D%22%23e8ecff%22%2F%3E%3Crect%20x%3D%2220%22%20y%3D%2220%22%20width%3D%22960%22%20height%3D%22120%22%20rx%3D%228%22%20fill%3D%22none%22%20stroke%3D%22%234f6bed%22%20stroke-width%3D%222%22%20stroke-dasharray%3D%228%206%22%2F%3E%3Ctext%20x%3D%22500%22%20y%3D%2288%22%20text-anchor%3D%22middle%22%20font-family%3D%22sans-serif%22%20font-size%3D%2222%22%20fill%3D%22%234f6bed%22%3EAn%20image%201000%20px%20wide%3C%2Ftext%3E%3C%2Fsvg%3E)
